facts.fact_text: The first applicant was born in 1984.
The second applicant was born in 1979.

According to the applicants, they read on various online social networks that many people intended to stage solo pickets (одиночные пикеты) on 19 December 2012 in front of the State Duma to express their opposition to the draft law prohibiting adoption of children of Russian nationality by US citizens.

According to the applicants, the format of solo pickets was chosen because there was no longer time to observe the minimum statutory three-day notification period required for other types of group public events.
The applicants decided to hold their own solo pickets on 19 December 2012.
At around 9 a.m. on 19 December 2012 the applicants positioned themselves, holding banners, in the vicinity of the State Duma at some distance from other protesters.
According to the applicants, they were arrested by the police several minutes after positioning themselves near the State Duma on 19 December 2012.
According to the applicants, they were brought to a police station after their arrest on 19 December 2012.
At 10.30 a.m. on 19 December 2012 the police drew up a record of administrative escorting (протокол административного доставления) in respect of each applicant.
A record of administrative arrest (протокол административного задержания) drawn up at 10.30 a.m. on 19 December 2012 stated that the applicants had arrived at the police station at 10.30 a.m.
The first applicant, Mr Tsukanov, made a handwritten note on his arrest record stating that he had been actually apprehended at 9.20 a.m. on 19 December 2012.
The second applicant, Mr Torchinskiy, made a handwritten note on his escorting record stating that he had been actually apprehended at 9.30 a.m. on 19 December 2012.

At the police station both applicants were accused of organising and holding a group public event without prior notification, in breach of Article 20.2 § 2 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO).
The administrative offence records indicate that the offences were committed at 10 a.m. on 19 December 2012.
The first applicant, Mr Tsukanov, made a handwritten note on his administrative offence record stating that he came to the event venue at 9 a.m. and was arrested at 9.20 a.m. on 19 December 2012.
The first applicant, Mr Tsukanov, was released from the police station at 1.20 p.m. on 19 December 2012.
The second applicant, Mr Torchinskiy, was released from the police station at 1.10 p.m. on 19 December 2012.

On 15 January 2013 the justice of the peace of the 369th Court Circuit of the Tverskoy District of Moscow found the second applicant, Mr Torchinskiy, guilty under Article 20.2 § 2 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO).

The justice of the peace of the 369th Court Circuit of the Tverskoy District of Moscow sentenced the second applicant, Mr Torchinskiy, to a fine of 20,000 Russian roubles (about 495 euros at the time of the judgment on 15 January 2013).

The justice of the peace found it established, on the basis of administrative records and testimony of police officers, that the second applicant, Mr Torchinskiy, had taken part in a picket involving fifty people on 19 December 2012.
The justice of the peace found that the picket on 19 December 2012 was unlawful because no notification had been submitted by the organisers as required by the Public Events Act (PEA).

The justice of the peace found that the second applicant, Mr Torchinskiy, had waved a banner during the picket on 19 December 2012, thereby attracting the attention of passers-by and journalists assembled for the occasion.
The justice of the peace found that the second applicant, Mr Torchinskiy, had not complied with the police order to stop picketing on 19 December 2012.

On 6 February 2013 the justice of the peace of the 369th Court Circuit of the Tverskoy District of Moscow found the first applicant, Mr Tsukanov, guilty under Article 20.2 § 2 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO).

The justice of the peace of the 369th Court Circuit of the Tverskoy District of Moscow sentenced the first applicant, Mr Tsukanov, to a fine of 20,000 Russian roubles (about 495 euros at the time of the judgment on 6 February 2013).
The reasoning in the judgment of 6 February 2013 concerning the first applicant, Mr Tsukanov, was identical to that in the judgment of 15 January 2013 concerning the second applicant, Mr Torchinskiy.

The justice of the peace in the judgment of 6 February 2013 also relied on police reports and testimony of a police officer who had apprehended the first applicant, Mr Tsukanov, at the venue of the public event on 19 December 2012.
Both applicants appealed against their respective convictions, insisting that each of them had held a solo demonstration which did not require prior notification of the authorities.
The first applicant, Mr Tsukanov, also pointed out in his appeal that he had been arrested earlier than indicated in the arrest record.
On 13 February 2013 the Tverskoy District Court of Moscow upheld the judgment concerning the second applicant, Mr Torchinskiy.
On 11 March 2013 the Tverskoy District Court of Moscow upheld the judgment concerning the first applicant, Mr Tsukanov.
The second applicant, Mr Torchinskiy, applied for review of the court decisions under Article 30.12 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO).
On 28 June 2013 the Deputy President of the Moscow City Court partly allowed the second applicant Mr Torchinskiy's complaint and changed the classification of the administrative charge against him.

On 28 June 2013 the Deputy President of the Moscow City Court found the second applicant, Mr Torchinskiy, guilty of breach of the established procedure for the conduct of public events committed by a participant, an offence punishable under Article 20.2 § 5 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO).
On 28 June 2013 the Deputy President of the Moscow City Court reduced the second applicant Mr Torchinskiy's fine to 10,000 Russian roubles (about 233 euros at the time).

At the police station both applicants were accused of organising and holding a group public event without prior notification, in breach of Article 20.2 § 2 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO).

On 15 January 2013 the justice of the peace of the 369th Court Circuit of the Tverskoy District of Moscow found the second applicant, Mr Torchinskiy, guilty under Article 20.2 § 2 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO).
The justice of the peace found that the picket on 19 December 2012 was unlawful because no notification had been submitted by the organisers as required by the Public Events Act (PEA).

A summary of domestic law and practice concerning regulations relating to the conduct of public events, liability for breaches committed in their course, and administrative escorting and arrest can be found in Lashmankin and Others v. Russia, nos. 57818/09 and 14 others, §§ 216-312, 7 February 2017.

A summary of domestic law and practice concerning regulations relating to the conduct of public events, liability for breaches committed in their course, and administrative escorting and arrest can also be found in Novikova and Others v. Russia, nos. 25501/07 and 4 others, §§ 47-85, 26 April 2016.
Since 6 January 2013 Moscow City Law no. 10 of 4 April 2007 provides that the distance between solo demonstrations should be no less than fifty meters.

Moscow City Law no. 10 of 4 April 2007 (as applicable since 6 January 2013) specifies in section 2.3 that simultaneous demonstrations should be treated as solo demonstrations provided that they do not have a common goal and organisation.
